findings.title: Construction Mechanic Basic, Chapter 8: Automotive Electrical Circuits and Wiring
findings.issuer: U.S. Navy / Center for Seabees and Facilities Engineering (chapter text attribution; government employee authorship not established by the chapter)
findings.publication_date: not stated in supplied chapter; PDF creation metadata 2014-06-10 is not a publication date
findings.technical_decision: candidate passages located; technical review pending. Procedures and voltage ranges require vehicle/manufacturer applicability checks. Regulator bypass is hazardous and should not become a generic learner instruction.
findings.verification_gap: Official course-list attribution and the chapter's Navy markings establish provenance; Navy copyright policy describes official-duty employee work, but chapter authorship and third-party text/figure provenance remain unverified. Obtain written publication-level confirmation or source documentation before classifying PUBLIC_DOMAIN. No excerpt may enter Ollama until rights clearance and technical review.

reviewed_sections.scope: alternator construction, regulator, maintenance, component testing
output, regulator, bypass and circuit resistance tests

artifact_observation.rights_observation: No copyright, license, individual author or employee-authorship statement found in supplied chapter. References on page 8-76 list third-party textbooks for further study; figures need individual provenance review.

provenance_review.official_catalog_observation: Navy Reserve FY25 course list identifies NAVEDTRA 14264A as Construction Mechanic Basic; supplied chapter identifies the Navy and CSFE.
provenance_review.rights_rule: SECNAVINST 5870.9 states works prepared by U.S. government officers or employees as official duties lack copyright protection. This does not prove the chapter's individual contributors or third-party inclusions.
provenance_review.artifact_rights_notice: No chapter-level license, author employment declaration, or figure rights notice found in supplied chapter.

candidate_claims_for_review.claim: Identify the battery, alternator, regulator, switch and indicator as charging circuit components.
candidate_claims_for_review.caveat: General architecture; modern integrated controls vary.

candidate_claims_for_review.claim: Explain stator AC generation, diode rectification, and field-current regulation.
candidate_claims_for_review.caveat: No figure reuse until individual figure provenance is cleared.

candidate_claims_for_review.claim: Use manufacturer specification when evaluating charging voltage at the battery.
candidate_claims_for_review.caveat: Avoid making one voltage threshold universal.

candidate_claims_for_review.claim: Contrast output/load testing with regulator voltage testing and follow-up checks.
candidate_claims_for_review.caveat: Historical vehicle examples and fixed 13.5–14.5 V range are not universal; require vehicle-specific technical review.

candidate_claims_for_review.claim: A voltage drop check can identify high resistance between alternator output and battery or along the ground return.
candidate_claims_for_review.caveat: Use vehicle-specific load and limit; do not present chapter's 0.7 V as universal.

excluded_for_generic_questions.reason: Regulator bypass/field jump procedure risks component damage and does not generalize to modern control systems.
Bench disassembly and diode test require component-specific process and safety review.
